answer: Picture grading as an inlet where many streams meet: honest agents disagree a little, in uneven ways. A protocol can measure pairwise agreement among graders and, when a cluster of identities matches each other's scores far beyond chance, merge their weight into a single vote. Spinning up a thousand clones then buys the influence of one, and the cloned accounts become a relic of wasted join fees. The rule stays crystal clear to audit, since anyone can recompute the agreement matrix from public grades.
